title: Game Development as Hobby Only
author: keytonw
selftext:
As I follow all the posts about anti-AI-game-dev and pushing back and etc, I keep being reminded of this amazing talk by Brandon Sanderson about The Philosophy of Professional Writing...

[https://www.brandonsanderson.com/blogs/blog/brandon-sandersons-writing-class-2025-week-1](https://www.brandonsanderson.com/blogs/blog/brandon-sandersons-writing-class-2025-week-1)

Sanderson points out an interesting double standard: nobody questions someone who plays basketball at their local gym about their NBA prospects, but mention you're writing a book and suddenly everyone wants to know about your publishing plans.

“It’s okay to be a non-professional writer,” he assures the class. “The primary purpose of art is to enrich your own life. Writing is good for you. It’s good for your soul. But because our society values utility, people often ask writers when they’ll ‘sell their book.’ You never hear someone playing basketball in a church gym being asked when they’re going to join the NBA.”

I am enjoying experimenting with game development. It feels very VERY much like I've always wanted to be a portrait painter and now -- finally -- there is a way for me to get past the first easy steps: slapping a face-shaped blob of paint onto the canvas and doing it really quickly. It sucks. Of course. It will suck for a long LONG time. But I can do it now.

Game development is like that for me...

I think I'm just going to make games for myself. If someone else plays them that'd be amazing. But if they don't I still love building and seeing my ideas take shape etc. I'm not ever going to make GTA 6 but then I'm never actually going to PLAY GTA 6, so it's ok.

Don't worry about the haters, folks. Just build and make art and "enrich your own life." And share!

Happy Friday, Y'all.

comments.author: CrowdGoesWildWoooo
comments.body:
I’ve seen a lot of “complain” posts in this sub. 

What I want to say if you want to make something as a passion project then sure go for it, but if you want to sell it, you better treat it as a business. Sometimes you need to adjust it to what the market wants.

Game dev Using AI already lowers the bar a lot but at the end of the day if it’s business it still requires investment, both can be money or effort. There’s noone holding you at a gunpoint to start a business, so stop acting like just because you pour effort to it, means like you are owed by the people to “respect” it. A business can flop, that’s just the reality of it.

comments.author: NephilimXXXX
comments.body:
I definitely disagree. I want people to enjoy the stuff i work on. This isn't just "for me". It's far too much time and work, and I'd rather spend my time doing something else if nobody was going to see it or enjoy it.

Imagine the scenario where you make a pie for your family. Everyone comes around and enjoys it. You like making the pie and sharing it with everyone and everyone enjoying it. Now imagine that you moved away to some new location. You can still make pie, but there's nobody around to share it with and nobody else to enjoy it. It's a much more hollow experience baking a pie and sharing it with nobody.

On a similar note, I wouldn't do all the work of writing a book if nobody else was going to read it.

A hobby doesn't mean you do it "just for yourself". It can mean "i enjoy doing it and sharing it with others and having them enjoy it too". The transition from hobby to a business venture is when you're making a living wage from it. Making money from it is also a useful way to spend more time doing it - because you aren't burdened with a day job to pay the bills.

comments.author: RustRoadsIO
comments.body:
I think it all comes down to expectations.

There are people who simply enjoy experimenting with tools (game engines, AI, Blender, etc.). Others want to express themselves and create something that other people might enjoy. And then there are those who want to make a living out of it. All of these approaches are equally valid.

The important thing to understand, though, is that AI is opening the door to much more competition. I think the game industry is going to be overcrowded for the next few years with games created through vibe coding. That's just reality.

When I took my first Unity course, almost a decade ago, just making a cube move or interact with the floor mesh could take several hours. Today, with AI, you can put together a 3D game with tons of features in a fraction of that time.

But here's the real question: does more content actually make a game more interesting? Does your game bring something new to the table, offer a different experience, or are you just recreating something that's already popular?

With or without AI, players are ultimately looking for one thing: fun. And at the end of the day, most players won't care how much AI you used to make your game. They'll care about whether they enjoy playing it.

So, by all means, experiment, create, and have fun. Just understand that making a game is becoming easier, but making a good and memorable game is still a completely different challenge.
